posts.name: Dalyodh Singh
posts.cooked:
I am not able to get how to call some name with abbr. using grep and $ if we have given some spaces at the end of his same
Examples

image1434×494 160 KB

Here I have given 12 spaces after name agampreet Singh

but if I use grep ‘gh’ with “$” it will not give me correct output
as there are 12 spaces after gh
how if someone ask me to identify name with end ‘gh’ and there are n spaces.

I use . 12 times because I know I have put 12 spaces after his final name

please @sayan look into it

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Let us break down your query into smaller pieces and try to solve it one at a time. This approach will help you solve future issues yourself.

  1. You want to match the string gh. You have already written the regex for that, which is gh.
  2. Now, you want to match space after it. Recall that the regex for whitespace is \s.
    You have used ., which matches any character, not just spaces, so gh. will match not only gh but also gho as well, since . matches any character. Lets replace that with a \s first.
❯ echo "gh " > somefile
❯ echo "gho" >> somefile
❯ grep 'gh' somefile
gh
gho
❯ grep 'gh$' somefile
❯ grep 'gh.' somefile
gh
gho
❯ grep 'gh\s$' somefile
gh

Observe that now we only match the line gh which has a space after it, and not gho.
3. Now we want to match not just a single space, but multiple spaces. There are two ways to do it.
a) If you know how many spaces to match, and want to match exactly 12 spaces, we can use grep -E 'gh\s{12}$ to match exactly 12 instances of spaces after gh and before the end of line.

❯ echo "one space " > somefile
❯ echo "two space  " >> somefile
❯ echo "three space   " >> somefile
❯ echo "four space    " >> somefile
❯ grep 'ce' somefile
one space
two space
three space
four space
❯ grep 'ce\s' somefile
one space
two space
three space
four space
❯ grep 'ce\s\s' somefile
two space
three space
four space
❯ grep 'ce\s$' somefile
one space
❯ grep 'ce\s\s$' somefile
two space
❯ grep 'ce\s\s\s$' somefile
three space
❯ grep -E 'ce\s{4}$' somefile
four space

However, here it is better to match any number of spaces after the gh till the end of line.

b) to match arbitrary number of spaces, we can use grep 'gh\s*' instead. It will match all lines that end with gh followed by any number of spaces (even zero).

❯ grep -E 'ce\s*$' somefile
one space
two space
three space
four space

Hope this clears things out. Also feel free to go through the resource book for System Commands where all these are explained and clarified in depth.

posts.name: Dalyodh Singh
posts.cooked:
thnx a lot brother
I use also this command

cat names.txt | grep ‘gh.*\s$’

It is working properly fine

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Glad to help.

Also,
cating into grep is redundant and slow. Prefer to pass the filename directly to grep.
